title: 价值≠价值感，很多人其实天生就有吸引力，只是很多人不敢做“自己”

timeline.summary: He defines attraction as consistency between inner state and outward behavior, then says being oneself is attractive only when the underlying self has value.
He says capable students can lose attraction by suppressing themselves and flattering women, while also insisting that self-development still requires effort.
He says reassurance is easy after attraction and gives hugging, future plans and positive messages as examples, then claims the same acts are seen as harassment without attraction.
After an editorial jump, he says nothing is a big deal while life remains, then advances an unverified belief that the soul is immortal and reincarnates.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He defines attraction as consistency, but says doing oneself is attractive only when the person already possesses what he calls value.
claims.conditions: His value hierarchy is undefined and uses a demeaning poverty example; it is not an objective ranking of people.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He says capable men can suppress their own behavior and lose attraction by performing deference or excessive protection, while effort remains necessary to develop attractive qualities.
claims.conditions: A broad relationship model, not proof that care or courtesy reduces attraction.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He presents a hug, a future plan and positive messages as reassurance after attraction, and claims the same acts are interpreted as harassment when attraction is absent.
claims.conditions: Attraction never substitutes for consent; hugs require freely given present permission, and messages or invitations must stop when unwelcome.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He says even death is not a major problem because he believes the soul is immortal and can reincarnate into a new body.
claims.conditions: Unverified spiritual belief; never use it to minimize death, grief, self-harm risk or medical danger.
